seoTitle: World Time Converter - Compare Timezones Globally
metaDescription: Convert time between multiple global timezones instantly. Compare the live current time or pick a specific date and time to see its equivalent worldwide.
intro: Do you need to know the exact current time in cities across the globe? Whether you are scheduling a call with colleagues in different countries, planning a live-stream for an international audience, or simply checking on a family member abroad, knowing the precise local time anywhere in the world is essential. Our World Time Converter displays the current live time for any city or time zone you select, updated in real time. It is the fastest way to see what time it is anywhere on the planet without having to mentally calculate offsets from your own local time. Everything runs directly in your browser using your device's clock, so there is no account needed and no data is ever sent to a server.
whatIs: The World Time Converter is a real-time utility that displays the current local time in any selected city or time zone around the world. Unlike a static time zone offset chart that requires you to manually add or subtract hours from UTC, this tool does all the work for you by tapping into your device's system clock and applying the appropriate UTC offset for the selected location. It supports all major world cities and IANA time zones, and it automatically handles Daylight Saving Time (DST) transitions so you always see the correct current time, even during spring-forward or fall-back periods. This makes it invaluable for remote workers, international businesses, frequent travelers, and anyone who regularly communicates across time zones.
howToUse: View the 'Live Time' mode to see a synchronized clock running for all selected cities.
Click 'Custom Time' to select a specific date and time.
Use the dropdown at the bottom to add more timezones, or click the trash icon to remove them.
howItWorks: The tool reads your browser's current date and time via the JavaScript Date API. When you select a target city or time zone, the converter applies the corresponding UTC offset—including any active DST adjustment—to calculate the exact local time at that location. The display updates every second so you are always looking at a live clock, not a stale snapshot. All time zone data is derived from the IANA Time Zone Database (also known as the Olson database), which is the authoritative global source for time zone rules, historical changes, and DST schedules. Because the calculation happens entirely in your browser, the result is instantaneous and your privacy is fully protected.
workedExample: Suppose it is currently 2:30 PM on October 1, 2026 in New York (EDT, UTC-4). You want to know the current time in Tokyo, Japan (JST, UTC+9). The offset difference is +13 hours. The converter adds 13 hours to 2:30 PM and displays 3:30 AM on October 2, 2026 in Tokyo. If you also check London (BST, UTC+1 during summer), the converter shows 7:30 PM on October 1, 2026. All of these conversions happen automatically and update every second, so you are always looking at the live current time in each city.
resultInterpretation: The displayed time is the exact current local time in the selected city or time zone, accounting for any active Daylight Saving Time adjustments. The date is also shown because a time zone difference can push the result into the next or previous calendar day. For example, when it is 11 PM Monday in New York, it is already 4 AM Tuesday in London. Always pay attention to the full date-and-time display to avoid scheduling errors that span midnight boundaries. If you need to compare multiple cities simultaneously, you can add several time zones to the display and see all of them update in real time.
useCases: International Meetings: Finding a suitable overlapping business hour for remote teams.
Travel Planning: Knowing exactly what time you will land at your destination.
Live Events: Converting a global broadcast time (like a sports match) to your local timezone.
tipsAndLimitations: Always double-check dates around the Spring/Fall boundaries, as Daylight Saving Time changes occur on different days for different countries.
The tool currently supports a curated list of major global timezone hubs.

faq.question: Does it automatically adjust for Daylight Saving Time (DST)?
faq.answer: Yes, by utilizing native browser timezone databases, all DST rules for the selected cities are applied automatically.

faq.question: Why is the day of the week different in some cities?
faq.answer: Because the Earth is divided into 24+ timezones, a city like Tokyo (GMT+9) is often a calendar day ahead of a city like Los Angeles (GMT-8).

disclaimer: Timezone rules are subject to change by local governments; this tool relies on your browser's updated timezone database for accuracy.
